title: Variables and Biases in Research
summary: Independent, dependent, extraneous variables; placebo effect; experimenter bias; participant bias; single-blind and double-blind designs.
objectives: Define independent, dependent and extraneous variables.
Explain placebo effect, experimenter bias and participant bias.
revision: IV manipulated, DV measured, extraneous uncontrolled. Placebo/experimenter/participant bias controlled by single/double-blind.
traps: Double-blind controls both experimenter and participant bias.
Placebo effect is improvement from belief, not treatment.
confusions: Believing extraneous variables are always controlled.

r: Uncontrolled variable that may affect results
Improvement due to belief in treatment, not the treatment itself
Participants alter behaviour knowing they are studied

i: Single-blind: participants do not know which group they are in.
Double-blind: neither participants nor researchers know who receives the treatment.

notes.t: Placebo effect, experimenter bias and participant bias are control issues frequently tested in UGC NET. Double-blind is the strongest control.

mnemonics.title: PEED
mnemonics.text: P — Placebo → placebo control, E — Experimenter → double-blind, E — Expectation → single-blind, D — Demand characteristics → deception
